current_round.prompt:
I've made changes to the Refine system so that this Goal should work much better. Please ignore previous rounds and implement:
For the web UI surface, create two new main nav right-aligned dropdown buttons, one for Skills and one for Sites. The right-aligned button order should be Skills, Sites, Settings, and New Goal. Yes, that is a rename of Controls to Settings. Move the menus from Settings (formerly Controls) to the appropriate new menu for Sites and Skills. Add a separator to the new menus for New Skill, New Site, Manage Skills, and Manage Sites. Ensure you use the standardized styles and layout we already have in the app.

goal.name: For the web UI surface, create two new main nav right-aligned dropdown buttons

checklist.description: Establish the navigation contract: the cause is that independent Skill and Site entry points are grouped inside Controls. The browser shell owns their placement and shared dropdown behavior; settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js already own their lists and actions. Preserve those owners and existing application capabilities. Update the checkout's navigation, Skills, and Knowledge Hub intent docs to describe the requested arrangement.

Update src/surfaces/web/static/index.html so the right-aligned actions appear in order: Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal. Move the existing Skill and Site containers into their respective dropdowns. Rename the Controls button and accessible label to Settings. Reuse shared summary, panel, icon, and menu-row styles from css/base.css; preserve the remaining settings controls and New Goal's related creation actions.

Update settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js to show existing entries followed by a separator and an action group: New Skill then Manage Skills, or New Site then Manage Sites. New actions open the existing creation modals; management links navigate to #/settings/skills and #/settings/knowledge-hub. Keep these actions available with empty lists, and render list failures separately from the action group. Preserve Skill eligibility, input preflight, agent-tab launch, and Site draft/published URL handling.

Bind each list's refresh-on-open listener to its new dropdown while retaining existing load, definition-change, and node-context refresh behavior and stale-response guards. Use common.js's shared topbar menu handling for mutual exclusion, action dismissal, outside clicks, and Escape. Extend shared selectors only where needed. Use shared border and spacing tokens for separators, and verify panels remain usable with long lists and narrow viewports.

Update user-facing navigation references in Guide, Skill help, reporter onboarding, and toolbar Todo copy to the new locations. Preserve existing route and element identities where practical, including Node and Reporter selectors, so the label change does not break shell integrations.

Update src/surfaces/web_server/tests/static_surface/navigation.rs and add focused browser coverage for action order, exclusive list placement, separators, all four create/manage actions, empty and failed lists, refresh after node or definition changes, Skill launch, and Site opening. Exercise keyboard operation, dismissal, light/dark themes, and desktop/narrow layouts. Proposed checks on the implementation derived from pinned base 9c1be94cf6421854a1c6693b7403b57d8f7576b2: cargo run --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml -- test-unit; node --test tests/web_topbar_navigation.test.js tests/web_knowledge_hub.test.js tests/web_node_scope_navigation.test.js tests/web_reporter_onboarding.test.js tests/web_theme.test.js. Require browser cases to execute rather than skip, and report failures separately from verified results.

Establish a reproducible failure baseline. Run each of the seven remaining Rust tests by exact name in separate processes on isolated checkouts of original base 9c1be94cf6421854a1c6693b7403b57d8f7576b2 and Round 2 base, then on the carried candidate. Use cargo test --lib <fully-qualified-test-name> -- --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1. Record executable provenance, relevant environment, exit codes, and failure identity. Separate independent failures from the shared-lock cascade; unchanged source alone does not prove baseline equivalence.

Correct the obsolete architecture expectation through its existing owner, src/architecture_tests.rs. Trace removal of workflow/recovery/quality against current workflow modules and runtime intent: Quality now uses explicit Error handling rather than automatic recovery Rounds. Replace the obsolete directory requirement with assertions for the actual supported responsibility after confirming history; do not recreate an empty directory or restore removed recovery behavior. Reconcile directly conflicting recovery documentation and verify architecture tests plus relevant workflow tests.

Repair the launch failure and environment-isolation cause behind the shared-lock cascade. Trace why the missing interpreter becomes exit 125 instead of the original OS error through the existing agent invocation and process-supervision owners. Preserve launch diagnostics and command/prompt cleanup. Make shared test environment restoration unwind-safe: the current test restores REFINE_SMOKE_AI_PATH only after assertions, so a panic can leak state and poison the lock used by the Events test. Verify both tests independently and together; merely tolerating a poisoned lock is insufficient.

Resolve the other four Rust failures against their governing invariants. Trace persistence-sync's unexpected run/ directory to runtime-path and repository-state ownership. For capture and redaction, distinguish valid structured launch-scope evidence from stale assertions while preserving replacement-registration fencing, process survival, and secret removal. Trace the Jira release-worker operation remaining Interrupted through existing operation settlement and orphan-exit ownership. Fix established production defects or strengthen stale tests to assert behavior. Use an environment workaround only with reproducible evidence that the same required behavior remains checked.

Verify the resulting candidate. Run cargo run --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml -- test-unit and cargo test --lib surfaces::web_server::tests::static_surface -- --test-threads=1. Run node --test tests/web_topbar_navigation.test.js tests/web_knowledge_hub.test.js tests/web_node_scope_navigation.test.js tests/web_reporter_onboarding.test.js tests/web_theme.test.js, plus the changed web_screen_render suite. Ensure browser tests execute without skips. Cover all four create/manage actions, empty/error lists, refresh and stale-response handling, Skill launch, Site opening, keyboard dismissal, menu exclusivity, light/dark themes, and long-list/desktop/narrow layouts. Preserve the corrected main-padding assertion. Run additional checks required by the effective workflow Skills; report failures and ignored tests explicitly.

Prepare the normal workflow handoff. Read the effective updated Implementation, Quality, and Governance Skill requirements before execution. Record evidence for every checklist ID, baseline comparisons, fixes, justified workarounds, and remaining limitations. Commit the scoped implementation on the Round 2 branch and report its exact candidate identity for independent Quality and Governance. Historical passes do not certify the new candidate; do not manually advance Goal state, approve, merge, or push.

skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For behavior changes, identify the underlying cause, governing concept or invariant, and existing owner before listing edits. Prefer strengthening an existing concept; introduce one only when it clarifies the behavior and reduces special cases. Do not change repository files. 

### Guidance

- Thrashing is a real danger with AI agents. To mitigate this, consider if the Goal is merely a symptom of a missing or misused concept in the target app architecture. Feel free to explore other Goals to determine if they have additional insights into this question.
- Over- or under-specificity can also cause undesirable implementation outcomes. Ensure that the plan has the information it needs for effective implementation, but not unnecessary details.
- Always use plain language.

### Format

Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

Example:
Task #1 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
Task #2 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
(etc.)

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.
